metadata.name: FromSpecs
metadata.description: Flow diagram > Drawn from the specs, checked against the flow tests. The screen-transition diagram since jsonui-cli 1.8.66: drawn from one source — each screen spec's `transitions[].destination`, plus `test.appOwnedScreens[].transitions` for a screen with no spec — with the flow tests checked against it rather than drawn from. Eight sections: why one source replaced two (a declaration with no reader), the closed vocabulary of destination kinds (screen / route / external / none / back / unknown) and what each draws, the resolution pipeline from prose to a screen id (case and separators, depth-counted parentheticals, splitting on or / slash / 、, aliases, multiple screens, parent and sub specs, `when`-gated siblings), the two declaration points in jui.config.json (`spec.transitionAliases` with a refused wrong position, `test.appOwnedScreens[].transitions`) and why aliases are per face, what the check accepts (forward edges and the return edge derived from `back`; back steps exempt; the three reasons; exit 1 after every page is written, outside `--allow-partial`), what is listed without being an error (unresolved as absent, inferred `none` at INFO, no spec directory as one warning, per-face counts), how to read the page (the All tab, groups, the ungrouped bucket, the `warnings N` closing line), and what the mechanism does not give. ~9-min read.

uiVariables.name: nextReadLinks
uiVariables.description: Three closing cards: testing (the files the check reads), screen identity (where a screen id comes from), navigation (how transitions are meant to be written).

notes: 2026-09-10 - Page created on the release that changed the rule, jsonui-cli 1.8.66, as the first article of a new top-level section. Every claim is taken from the library's own canon (`shared/core/screen_identity.json`, `diagram` section) and from the upstream release record, with the reporting projects' names, screen names and per-project counts left out; the four unresolved rates quoted in section 6 are the canon's own figures. Three things on the page were checked against the shipped 1.8.66 tree rather than transcribed: the kind the classifier assigns to each example destination, the field names of an `appOwnedScreens` object entry, and the format of the `ERROR [doc-diagram]:` line and the closing `warnings N` line. This site does not run `generate html` or `generate mermaid` itself, so the exit-1 behaviour is stated from the canon's `flowTestCheck.severity` and the upstream acceptance, not from a run here — the site's own gates regenerate spec and component documents only.
